gettingstarted.title: Getting started with the map
gettingstarted.markdownText:
## Getting started with the map

If you're new to the map or using spatial data, our Getting Started video quickly covers the basic functionality you'll need to use to add and interrogate data sets.

If you don't have time to watch the video, we suggest exploring the following areas:

1. Search for a location to quickly find an area of interest
2. Use 'Explore map data' to view the catalogue of available data sets and add them to the map
3. Interact with the data layer, including opacity and toggling on and off on the left in your workbench
4. Click on the data on the map to view more detailed data, including the raw data
5. Change your basemap using options in 'Map Settings' to help make some data sets more visible
6. Zoom and change your view, including tilting the view angle using the controls on the right-hand side of the screen

stepbystepguide.title: Step by step guide
stepbystepguide.markdownText:
## Step by step guide

Launch a step by step guide for various popular workflows below:

step1.markdownDescription: The search is at the top of the workbench on the left.
step1.title: Search for a location to find an area of interest

step2.markdownDescription: You can view the catalogue at any time
step2.title: Use "Explore map data" to view data catalogue

step3.title: Search for data or browse catalogue

step4.title: Add data to map by clicking on + sign or "Add to map" button in preview window

step5.title: Interact with data, including opacity and toggling on & off on the left in your workbench

step6.title: Click on data on the map to view more details by triggering Feature Information panel

step7.title: Change your basemap using options in "Map Settings" to improve contrast

step8.title: Zoom and change view using the controls on the right-hand side of the screen

satelliteimagery.title: Adding satellite imagery
satelliteimagery.footnote: Important: Satellite imagery can take a little while to load so please be patient. If images don’t seem to be loading, zoom out a little bit

step1.title: Find the location to view satellite imagery
step1.markdownDescription: - Use the location search or zoom and pan around the map using your mouse or the zoom controls

step2.title: Add the satellite imagery to the map
step2.markdownDescription:
- Open the data catalogue using "Explore map data" button
- Navigate through datasets to select your satellite option: Landsat or Sentinel, and daily or composite images. This can depend on resolution of the image you need (10m or 25m) and whether you want daily, 16 day composite, or annual average images
 - Select "Add to the map" to view the satellite imagery

step3.title: Filter images to find satellite imagery
step3.markdownDescription:
- Filter images by location to quickly find satellite images for that location
 - Satellites circle the globe many times a day. You can expect satellite imagery to be available for one location every two weeks
 - If you haven't already selected your point of interest on the map, zoom in to select one. You will see the filter applied in blue in the Workbench on the left

step4.title: Select a time and date
step4.markdownDescription:
- Use the date picker to select a time and date. Cycle backwards through previous years using the back arrow
 - Choose another date if your imagery is obscured by clouds. You can quickly cycle back and forward using the arrows next to the date picker

comparetimeseries.title: View and compare different points in time
comparetimeseries.footnote: Important: Any time series data can be compared using the Split Screen Mode, not just satellite imagery

step1.title: Add a time series dataset to the map
step1.markdownDescription:
- Satellite imagery is a good example of time series data, with many satellites going back decades
- Find your location of interest and filter available imagery by this location
-See our Adding Satellite Imagery to the Map guide for more

step2.title: Select the time and date
step2.markdownDescription:
- In the workbench on the left, select the time and date which will open the date picker
- Select a year, month and date, or navigate back to other years and even centuries using the back arrow
- Available dates appear in blue

step3.title: Compare different dates at one location
step3.markdownDescription:
- From the 3 dots drop-down menu in the workbench, press 'Compare' to activate Split Screen Mode
- A duplicate copy of your dataset will appear in the workbench
- Choose the dates you want to compare on the left and right of the screen
- Drag the slider using the white button to swipe and compare the two image dates

step4.title: Close Split Screen Mode
step4.markdownDescription:
- Escape the Split Screen Mode by pressing the 'x' of Split Screen Mode title in the workbench
- Remove the duplicate copy of your dataset in the workbench using the 3 dots drop-down menu

helpContentTerm1.content: A collection of related information, organised as one using a common data structure, e.g. "average house prices in Sydney for 2019" or "minimum and maximum daily temperature"

helpContentTerm2.content: A sequence of data collected over different points in time, e.g. temperature sensor data or a gallery of images of the same location

helpContentTerm3.content: The panel on the left side of the screen that shows what datasets you have added to the map

helpContentTerm4.content: 3D data that also has a time-series component

helpContentTerm5.content: the inventory of all datasets available to be added to the map

helpContentTerm6.content: Different map options for the blank base map, such as Bing imagery, roads, dark or light maps

helpContentTerm7.content: The dataset you added to your workbench that allows for difference calculations

helpContentTerm8.content: The way the dataset appears in the preview window. We recommend true colour to search for cloud-free images

population.name: Population by marz, 2021
population.description:
Population of Armenia by marz (province) and sex, 2021 estimates.

Source: [Armenia - Subnational Population Statistics](https://data.opendata.am/dataset/armenia-subnational-population-statistics), Open Data Armenia (OCHA common operational dataset).

worldpop.name: Population distribution, 2020 (WorldPop, ~100 m)
worldpop.description:
Estimated number of people per ~100 m cell in 2020 (WorldPop constrained). Cells without buildings are empty.

Source: [WorldPop](https://data.opendata.am/dataset/wdwp-49747), CC BY 4.0. Coloured for the atlas by `scripts/population/build.sh`.

kontur.name: Population in 400 m hexagons (Kontur)
kontur.description:
Population of 400 m H3 hexagons, 2022.

Source: [Kontur Population](https://data.opendata.am/dataset/armenia-population-density-for-400m-h3-hexagons), CC BY 4.0.

rwi.name: Relative Wealth Index (Meta)
rwi.description:
Relative standard of living within Armenia at 2.4 km resolution, estimated from satellite imagery, connectivity and survey data. Higher values mean wealthier areas.

Source: [Data for Good at Meta](https://data.opendata.am/dataset/armenia-relative-wealth-index), CC BY-SA.

settlements.name: Settlements
settlements.description:
Settlements in Armenia from OpenStreetMap, exported monthly by the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team.

Source: [HDX](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hotosm_arm_populated_places), © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.

earthquakes.name: Earthquakes since 1970, M3+ (USGS)
earthquakes.description:
Earthquakes of magnitude 3 and above in Armenia and nearby since 1970, from the USGS catalog. New events appear automatically.

Source: [USGS Earthquake Hazards Program](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/), public domain.

infrastructure.healthDescription:
Hospitals, clinics, pharmacies and dentists in Armenia from healthsites.io, based on OpenStreetMap.

Source: [Healthsites of Armenia](https://data.opendata.am/dataset/healthsites-of-armenia), CC BY-SA.

financial.name: Banks, ATMs and other financial services

Banks, ATMs and other financial services in Armenia from OpenStreetMap, exported monthly by the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team.

Source: [HDX](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hotosm_arm_financial_services), © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.

airports.name: Airports
airports.description:
Airports in Armenia from OpenStreetMap, exported monthly by the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team.

Source: [HDX](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hotosm_arm_airports), © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.

railways.name: Railways

infrastructure.name: Infrastructure and services

gbif.name: Species observations (GBIF)
gbif.description:
Density of species occurrence records in Armenia: observations, museum specimens and surveys published to GBIF (about 390,000 records). Brighter colour means more records.

Source: [GBIF.org](https://www.gbif.org/country/AM/summary), data from many publishers under CC0, CC BY and CC BY-NC.

yerevan.name: Yerevan
yerevan.description: Layers of the [Yerevan Municipality GIS](https://gis.yerevan.am/server/rest/services). The municipality does not state a licence for these data; they are shown with attribution to the source.

airQuality.description: Hourly mean concentration of fine particulate matter PM2.5 (µg/m³) at the sensors of the Yerevan air quality network. Sensors without readings in the last 24 hours are hidden. For comparison, the WHO guideline for the daily mean is 15 µg/m³.
airQuality.name: Air quality: PM2.5, last hour

odam.name: Open Data Armenia: datasets for the atlas
odam.description: Datasets of [data.opendata.am](https://data.opendata.am) tagged `atlas`, loaded from the catalogue when the map opens. Tag a dataset `atlas` to add it here.

intro.title: Armenia in maps
intro.text: Armenia is divided into 11 marzes (provinces), including the capital Yerevan, where more than a third of the population lives. This story shows what the atlas can tell about the country: people, natural hazards, water, climate and nature. Use the arrows to move between scenes.

people.title: Where people live
people.text: Population estimated for every ~100 m cell (WorldPop) shows how people concentrate in the Ararat valley, around Lake Sevan and along the river valleys of the north and south. The high mountains are almost empty.

yerevan.title: Yerevan
yerevan.text: The capital's 12 administrative districts, metro stations and the city's air quality network. The coloured dots show the hourly concentration of fine particulate matter PM2.5 measured by about 200 sensors.

seismic.title: A seismic country
seismic.text: Armenia lies in one of the most seismically active parts of the Caucasus. The map shows the probabilistic seismic hazard, active faults and earthquakes of magnitude 3 and above recorded since 1970.

spitak.title: Spitak, 7 December 1988
spitak.text: The magnitude 6.8 Spitak earthquake destroyed Spitak and badly damaged Leninakan (now Gyumri) and Kirovakan (now Vanadzor). At least 25,000 people died. The points show where damage photographs were taken.

water.title: Water
water.text: Rivers, their catchments, lakes and reservoirs. Lake Sevan, about 1,900 m above sea level, is the largest lake in the Caucasus and the country's main reserve of fresh water.

climate.title: Climate
climate.text: Average annual precipitation ranges from about 200–300 mm in the Ararat valley to 800 mm and more in the mountains. Explore the Climate group for temperature, solar radiation and wind resources.

nature.title: Biodiversity
nature.text: About 390,000 observations of plants, animals and fungi in Armenia have been published to GBIF. Brighter areas have more records: they show where nature is studied most, not only where it is richest.

data.title: Open data
data.text: All layers of the atlas come from open sources, and many are published on data.opendata.am. Open the data catalogue to find more layers, or tag a dataset atlas on data.opendata.am to add it to the map.

welcomeMessage.title: Atlas of Armenia
welcomeMessage.welcomeMessage:
Explore open data about Armenia on the map: population, natural hazards, water, climate, nature and the city of Yerevan.
Start with the story, browse the data catalogue or search for a place.
